factual_methodological.summary: The lead data were rechecked against same-day primary releases from China's National Bureau of Statistics, the Australian Bureau of Statistics and the UK Office for National Statistics; the RBA policy rate was checked against the 29 September Monetary Policy Board release. Diffusion indices, inflation rates and GDP growth are kept dimensionally separate and the cross-country table explicitly warns that levels are not comparable.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Opening is finding-led, analytical headings identify mechanisms, EN and PT-BR are idiomatic, the 30 September strict public-prose gate finds no QA/pipeline/template/self-reference language, and the conclusion synthesizes new information rather than repeating an internal checklist.

novelty_against_previous_daily.summary: Compared with 27-29 September, the lead thesis changes materially: 29 September established Australia-China policy divergence; 30 September tests that split with new official PMI, CPI and UK national-accounts data and distinguishes Chinese production improvement from labour/demand breadth.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 Markdown table + 1 explicit line chart + 1 causal flow per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The brief meets the required visual floor. The China PMI chart uses official monthly values; the cross-country table labels heterogeneous units and states they are not level-comparable; EN/PT-BR visual signatures and values are equivalent.

contextual_depth.summary: Context from the prior day's policy split is used only to interpret same-day data. The article separates production, employment, domestic demand, headline versus underlying inflation and revised versus current growth evidence.

political_neutrality.summary: Policy decisions are described as institutional facts and macroeconomic transmission mechanisms; no political actor, government or policy choice is endorsed, ranked or opposed.

contrary_evidence: China's headline manufacturing PMI returned above 50, but employment, small-firm conditions, non-manufacturing new orders and existing manufacturing orders remain below the expansion threshold.
Australian headline CPI accelerated, but trimmed-mean inflation was unchanged at 3.6%, so the release does not establish a fresh acceleration in underlying inflation.
The UK GDP revision is backward-looking and does not by itself establish the third-quarter trajectory or eliminate the constraint from high financing costs.
limitations: China PMI indicators are diffusion indices and should not be interpreted as growth or inflation rates.
Australia's August monthly CPI can be influenced by volatile fuel and administered-price effects; the article separates headline from trimmed-mean inflation.
UK quarterly national accounts are revised estimates and remain subject to future revisions.
Same-day European and U.S. releases available later on 30 September may add information after the stated 08:00 BRT cutoff.
notes: Approved for publication after same-day primary-source recheck, exact SHA binding, three-edition novelty comparison, bilingual review and visual-semantic validation.

en.title: Global Macro — China returns to expansion as Australian inflation reaccelerates
en.deck: China's manufacturing PMI returned to 50.1 while Australia's CPI accelerated to 4.0% and UK second-quarter growth was revised to 0.5%, turning policy divergence into measurable macro divergence.
en.regime: Data-confirmed policy dispersion: Chinese activity has moved back above the expansion threshold but labour and parts of demand remain weak, while Australian inflation has reaccelerated and UK growth has been revised higher.
en.key_risk: If China's production rebound fails to broaden into employment and internal demand while Australia and other economies retain inflation pressure, policy and market dispersion can widen further instead of converging toward a common global cycle.

pt-BR.title: Global Macro — A China volta à expansão enquanto a inflação australiana acelera
pt-BR.deck: O PMI industrial da China voltou a 50,1, enquanto o CPI australiano acelerou para 4,0% e o crescimento britânico do segundo trimestre foi revisado para 0,5%, transformando divergência de política em divergência macroeconômica mensurável.
pt-BR.regime: Dispersão de política confirmada pelos dados: a atividade chinesa voltou acima do limite de expansão, mas trabalho e partes da demanda permanecem fracos, enquanto a inflação australiana reacelerou e o crescimento britânico foi revisado para cima.
pt-BR.key_risk: Se a retomada da produção chinesa não se ampliar para emprego e demanda interna enquanto Austrália e outras economias mantêm pressão inflacionária, a dispersão de política e mercados pode aumentar em vez de convergir para um ciclo global comum.
